system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.
user:
Issuer: Demo national authority (stands in for the real issuer)
Context: real event
Target area (chosen by the operator): Western region (demo zone)

Event inputs:
1. [verified; NCM via WAM, 2026-02-17, https://www.wam.ae/en/article/bysbij4-fog-alert-uae-motorists-warned-low-visibility] ABU DHABI, February 17, 2026 (WAM) – The National Center for Meteorology (NCM) has issued a weather warning regarding potential fog formation and significantly reduced horizontal visibility across several western regions of the UAE. According to the NCM statement released on Tuesday, visibility is expected to deteriorate—and may drop to zero at times—starting from 21:30 tonight until 10:00 AM Wednesday, February 18. The Center has urged motorists to exercise extreme caution on the roads. Drivers are advised to follow all traffic safety guidelines, maintain a safe distance from other vehicles, and strictly adhere to modified speed limits, particularly in areas experiencing thick fog.
2. [verified; issuer profile] Issuer public site (demo): https://alerts.example.ae
3. [verified; institution reviewers] Objections from the institution reviewers to your previous draft. Fix what is within the verified inputs; do not add facts: Met office reviewer objects (description): The description overstates the hazard. NCM warns of 'potential fog formation' and mentions thick fog only for 'areas experiencing thick fog'. It does not say thick fog is expected across the western regions. Fix: Replace 'thick fog is expected in western regions of the UAE' with 'fog may form in several western regions of the UAE, thick in places', which keeps to the bulletin wording. | Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): Both language versions exceed the UAE handset requirement of a single cell broadcast page. English (218 characters, GSM-7) takes 3 pages and Arabic (228 characters, UCS-2) takes 6. Fix: Cut each text to fit one page. That means about 93 characters for English in GSM-7 and about 41 characters for Arabic in UCS-2, since one page is 82 usable octets. Keep only the hazard, area, time and action. Drop the long date phrasing and possibly the URL, or shorten them. If a one-page Arabic UCS-2 text cannot carry the essential content, a person should decide whether to accept it. [cites Regulatory Update: New cell handset requirements in UAE (summary of TRA Technical Specification TS040), requirement 3] | Network operator and regulator reviewer objects (phone_text): The protective action ('Drive with extreme caution' / 'قُد بحذر شديد') sits near the end of both texts. On a multi-page delivery the first page carries only the hazard and timing, not the action. Fix: Restructure both texts so the hazard and the action appear at the very start. For example: 'Thick fog W. UAE tonight–Wed 10:00: drive with extreme caution.' Put the same order in the Arabic text.

data.headline: Fog may cut visibility to zero in western UAE, 21:30 Tue to 10:00 Wed 18 Feb
data.description: Fog may cut visibility to zero, W. UAE, 21:30 Tue-10:00 Wed: drive with extreme caution.
data.instruction: Drive with extreme caution, keep a safe distance from other vehicles and follow the modified speed limits, especially where fog is thick. More information: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so none were excluded.
Following the Met office objection, 'thick fog expected' was not used. The bulletin only says fog may form, and it mentions thick fog only for some areas.
The URL and the full date phrasing were removed from the phone text so it fits one GSM-7 page (88 characters, under about 93). The URL remains in the instruction.
An Arabic phone text was not drafted because this task asks for English only. The Arabic single-page limit of about 41 UCS-2 characters still needs a human decision.
data.note_for_reviewer: 'W. UAE' shortens NCM's 'several western regions' to fit one page; please confirm this matches the operator's demo zone. Severity is set to Moderate and certainty to Likely ('expected to deteriorate', with fog 'potential'); please confirm, and assign the Arabic one-page text to a person as the regulator reviewer requested.
